newsitem.title: UK: Britain's BT mulls call charge move - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain's BT mulls call charge move - paper.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) is considering offering "free local calls" for domestic customers coupled with higher line rental charges in a move that could transform Internet use in Britain, the Independent newspaper said on Monday.
A spokesman for BT said the company is looking at a range of possible new packages in its campaign to counter competition from Mercury Communications and cable companies according to the Independent.
One route would be to slash charges for local calls and charge a higher quarterly line rental instead.
Internet access is charged at local call rates and many observers fear that Internet usage in the UK has been hampered by BT's local charges, the Independent said.
In the U.S., individuals benefit from packages that offer "free" local calls coupled with a premium line rental charge.
